Oppressed by the two, the gods came to Himavat and saluted the Mother of all beings, the giver of desires.
She sits on the lovely peak of Himavat, riding a lion, served on every side by daughters of the gods with folded hands.
One massages her feet, another dresses her hair; one massages her hands, another has put collyrium on her eyes.
One, holding a mirror in her hand, shows her her face; one gives her betel with cloves, cardamom and the like.
One friend stands before her holding a spittoon; another adorns all her limbs with ornaments, garments and the like.
Her thighs are like plantain stems, her nose like a parrot's, her arms like creepers; her feet have tinkling anklets and she wears a lovely girdle.
Her breasts sway beneath a pearl necklace fragrant with gleaming musk; her neck shines with a necklace, and she is adorned with swinging garlands.
